subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram quote/reply context should be a first-class, durable inbound contract instead of a split prompt/runtime patch surface

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the structured runtime-context shape proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90745 as the canonical cross-channel reply contract, with Telegram fixtures as the acceptance boundary?
rationale: The existing documentation selects the high-level prompt-versus-metadata split, but maintainers still need to choose the durable cross-runtime and cross-channel field contract before a broad issue can be considered complete.

options.title: Sponsor structured runtime metadata
options.body: Adopt the runtime-context approach, require Telegram reply and selected-quote regression fixtures, and keep outbound Quote-UI compatibility in its separate issue.

options.title: Define a narrower Telegram-only contract
options.body: Keep reply facts channel-local for now and document the supported Telegram fields without committing to a generic runtime contract.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Leave the existing behavior as-is and close only narrow independently reproducible bugs, accepting that cross-channel consistency remains unresolved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor structured runtime metadata
recommendation.body: Adopt the runtime-context approach, require Telegram reply and selected-quote regression fixtures, and keep outbound Quote-UI compatibility in its separate issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is connected to the only active implementation proposal covering the central runtime handoff, though final API direction requires broader maintainer approval.
